evidence: Varr. RR 2.6.4: asinum, bovem ab opere (sc. disjungere; Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The opposite of conjungere, as unyoking is of yoking; its use for taking a plug out is modern, and ours. Traupman has adnectere for plugging in (see “plug in”) and nothing for the reverse.

terms.gloss: pull out: pull out the plug
evidence: Plaut. Rud. 4.4.124: rēte ex aquā (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Replētrum disjunge: tēlephōnum jam plēnum est.
phrases.english: Unplug the charger: the phone’s fully charged.
Pull out the plug before you fix the lamp.

sources: Lewis & Short: disjungo · Lewis & Short: extraho
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 124.
